attachesAs: hamza ABOVE a tooth carrier, added after the word's main line
compositionOrder: write the tooth carrier as part of the word's right-to-left main line
after lifting, add the small hamza above the carrier as its ain-head shape or accepted diagonal squiggle

compositionSource.citation: Zer o Zabar, Ain and hamza, initial and medial ئ handwriting animations and Hamza instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026)
compositionSource.variation: The lesson prints initial ئـ and medial ـئـ, shows separate handwriting animations for both, and explains that Urdu hamza uses a be-series tooth carrier in these positions. Its prose identifies hamza's vowel-separator role with بھائی among the examples and permits the small ain-head mark to be smoothed into a diagonal squiggle. The course therefore models ئ as a source-backed carrier-plus-mark composition rather than inventing a standalone Arabic ي row: write the right-to-left main-line carrier first, then return after a lift to add hamza. Unicode canonically decomposes U+0626 into U+064A plus U+0654; those code points identify the encoded composition and do not conflate Urdu ی U+06CC with Arabic ي U+064A.
